explanation: Retrospective mid-word readout: N2281+ fires on a token that leaves the current orthographic word unfinished and that the model will not end there - at its strong firings the next-token distribution puts 0.80-1.00 of its mass on word-internal fragments (scan mean 0.26) with essentially none on a space, and firing is four times commoner on non-word-final tokens (1.13% vs 0.28%). The strength is then set by the fragment itself: it saturates at 6-8.5 on bare Graeco-Latin stems that cannot stand alone and need a later token to resolve (' neph' 6.3, 'ceph' 7.2, ' tele' 5.1, ' qu' 4.9, 'pharmac' 3.8, 'ther' 4.0, ' ph' 4.4, ' hepat' 2.1, ' kil' 2.4), and sits at the 0.16 floor both when the tokenizer keeps the word whole ('encyclopedia', 'pharmacist', 'televised', 'broadcast', 'notwithstanding') and, mostly, when the word's leading piece is already a complete English word (' counter'+intuitive, ' photos'+ynthesis, ' polymer'+ase, ' electro'+cardiogram); it prepares no particular upcoming token (Jacobian kurtosis 3.3, promoted list incoherent, zero-ablation KL ~2e-5). Left unexplained: about a tenth of the strong firings land on word-final tokens, chiefly ' triple' and ' single' as stacked premodifiers ('two triple expansion engines', 'single player'), and a few bare stems such as ' arter'+iosclerosis and ' mitochond'+rion stay quiet.
